newsitem.title: USA: "Jenny Jones" lawyers fuming over deposition.
newsitem.headline: "Jenny Jones" lawyers fuming over deposition.

text.p: A lawyer for talk show host Jenny Jones was fuming Friday over the release of a videotaped deposition in which Jones said she misled convicted murder Jonathan Schmitz about her fateful show on same-sex secret crushes.

Flamboyant Detroit-area attorney Geoffrey Fieger, who is suing "The Jenny Jones Show" and its producers for $25 million in damages on behalf of Scott Amedure's family, distributed edited excerpts of the 2.5-hour deposition Thursday.
Schmitz was convicted in November of murdering Amedure in 1995, three days after Amedure revealed a crush on him during the taping of a "Jenny Jones" segment on same-sex secret crushes.
In the deposition, Jones said she did not know what Schmitz was told about the show, but said she did not want him to know that his "secret crush" was a man.
"I cared that he not know, otherwise we wouldn't have had a show," Jones said.
Jones said it was the practice of the show to withhold some information from guests who agree to appear on shows in which they learn on camera the identity of a person who has affections for them.
"When you do a secret crush show, you don't give full disclosure," Jones said.
Jones said she could remember little about what was said to and about Schmitz in preparation for the show.
Fieger told the Oakland Press that Jones was a "prevaricating liar."
J. Michael Huget, the Detroit attorney who is representing the show and its producer, Warner Brothers' Telepictures Productions, said the release of the tape was "highly inappropriate."
"Fieger's obviously worried that the case will not stand up in court, so he has to resort to selectively edited soundbites," Huget said.
Huget said he intends to prove that Schmitz was responsible for his own actions.
"We intend to show that from Schmitz' own actions, he knew his crush could be a man or a woman and he willingly came on the show with this knowledge," Huget said.
